2026-09-01
Por Capturas de pantalla
**By Albert Samaha**
May 30, 2026
The night Italy defeated France in the 2006 World Cup final, Mario de Rossi was studying at a small university in Puglia. Though he had exams the next day, he still ventured out into a piazza afterward and celebrated late into the night. He showed up to his exams bleary-eyed, and wearing his Azzurri shirt. With four World Cup titles, Italy had, at that point, more than any other European country. “Back then, we were at the center of the football world,” de Rossi, now a forty-year-old football agent who specializes in international player transfers, told me. “And to think that from there a decline began that now feels almost irreversible.”

item.title: Sony accuses Anthropic of 'brazen campaign' to train Claude on its music — and wants up to $150,000 a song
item.author: Lauren Edmonds
item.description:
Sony accuses Anthropic of 'brazen campaign' to train Claude on its music — and wants up to $150,000 a song
2026-09-01
Por Lauren Edmonds
https://businessinsider.com/anthropic-claude-training-copyright-music-lyrics-sony-lawsuit-2026-8
Sony Music and Warner Chappell want Anthropic to pay up.
The publishing companies filed a lawsuit against Anthropic in a Northern California district court on Friday. Anthropic cofounders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann were also named in the filing.
Anthropic denied the accusations in a statement. "We disagree with the publishers' claims and we intend to defend ourselves robustly in court," the company said.
Sony Music and Warner Chappell requested a jury trial. They're seeking statutory damages from Anthropic, including up to $150,000 for each composition it used to train Claude.
"Even the most revolutionary of technologies must develop within the bounds of the law, and Anthropic's Claude models are no different," the companies said in the complaint.
Tech companies need troves of data to train their AI models, and go to great lengths to acquire it. Most recently, historians and archivists have accused AI companies of acquiring large numbers of antique books and feeding them into their LLMs, destroying them in the process.

item.title: The Global War for Capital
item.author: Audio propio
item.description:
The Global War for Capital
2026-09-01
Por Audio propio
Las fuentes analizan la volatilidad de los mercados financieros durante agosto de 2026, destacando el impacto de la inteligencia artificial, el conflicto con Irán y las decisiones de la Reserva Federal. Se detalla cómo el gobierno estadounidense ha expandido su portafolio accionario hacia empresas de semiconductores, mientras que grandes tecnológicas como Microsoft y Nvidia muestran resultados mixtos frente a la presión de los rendimientos de los bonos. El sector energético enfrenta una fuerte inestabilidad en los precios del petróleo, lo que complica las metas de inflación y las expectativas de las tasas de interés. Por otro lado, la salud del consumidor se ve afectada por una economía debilitada y un mercado inmobiliario estancado, lo que influye en el desempeño de minoristas y empresas de servicios. Finalmente, se examina el auge de las ofertas públicas iniciales en el sector restaurantero y la tendencia de los inversores a refugiarse en efectivo ante la incertidumbre global.

item.title: Estas son las versiones, chats, pericias y seguimientos que vincularían a José Serrano con el asesinato de Fernando Villavicencio
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
Estas son las versiones, chats, pericias y seguimientos que vincularían a José Serrano con el asesinato de Fernando Villavicencio
2026-09-01
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/jose-serrano-asesinato-fernando-villavicencio-versiones-chats-pericias-seguimientos-131518/
Estas son las versiones, chats, pericias y seguimientos que vincularían a José Serrano con el asesinato de Fernando Villavicencio
El exministro José Serrano fue recluido en la Cárcel del Encuentro tras su deportación desde Estados Unidos. Expedientes policiales y peritajes telefónicos detallan presuntos seguimientos de inteligencia, aportes económicos y maniobras de encubrimiento en torno al crimen de Fernando Villavicencio que relacionarían al exministro.
El exministro del correísmo José Serrano en su nueva celda de la cárcel del Encuentro, de Santa Elena, el sábado 29 de agosto de 2026.
- Foto
Gobierno Ecuador
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
El viernes 28 de agosto de 2026, a las 23:09, un jet ejecutivo procedente de Miami tocó la pista del aeropuerto de Guayaquil. A bordo viajaba el exministro del Interior José Ricardo Serrano Salgado, entregado a las autoridades ecuatorianas por agentes de Seguridad Nacional de Estados Unidos.
El traslado se realizó desde el aeropuerto de Opa-locka (KOPF), en el condado de Miami-Dade, en una aeronave ejecutiva Challenger CL-35 con matrícula estadounidense N41VD. La tripulación estuvo al mando del capitán Carlos Eslava y del copiloto Bryan Bernal.
La custodia del exministro estuvo a cargo de cuatro agentes de Investigaciones de Seguridad Nacional de Estados Unidos (HSI, por sus siglas en inglés): Steven Arthur George, Rex Douglas Wiegers, Jason Scott Ahwee y Carlos Moreno Jr.
Al descender del avión, Serrano fue puesto a disposición del personal de la Unidad Nacional de Investigación con la Fiscalía General (UNIF), junto a los funcionarios migratorios.
En el acta de entrega migratoria se adjuntó su pasaporte ecuatoriano y se inventariaron sus bienes: un billete de USD 1 y una moneda de 10 centavos estadounidenses, dos etiquetas de equipaje aéreo a su nombre con prendas personales, un collar tipo rosario de plástico negro, un estuche de lentes rosado con armazón café y un anillo de metal dorado con la inscripción interna grabada "Maria Paula".

item.title: Alphabet stock has tanked to close out the summer because of a 'brain drain' — what may happen to it next
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Alphabet stock has tanked to close out the summer because of a 'brain drain' — what may happen to it next
2026-09-01
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/alphabet-stock-has-tanked-to-close-out-the-summer-because-of-a-brain-drain--what-may-happen-to-it-next-102219947.html
The humans departing Alphabet (GOOGL) are also taking a piece of the tech beast's stock price with them.
Shares of Alphabet are down 6% over the past month versus a 3% advance for the S&P 500 (^GSPC), per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
"There's two debates that are weighing on Alphabet shares," Eric Sheridan, business unit leader of the TMT Group within Goldman Sachs Research, said on Yahoo Finance's Opening Bid (video above). "One, is that search slowed down a little bit more than investors expected [in the second quarter]."
"The second bigger theme that's weighed on it is there's been brain drain," Sheridan continued. "There's been departures from folks at Gemini, Google, DeepMind, Google broadly, and Gemini's next generation model has been delayed — the 3.5 Pro. And now they're talking about Gemini four. We've seen this with other companies. Meta went through it 12, 15 months ago when they ripped up the playbook and started spending billions."
Several of the more prominent names at Alphabet that have left or seen their roles reshuffled include Demis Hassabis and Jeff Dean.
Hassabis is now the former CEO of Google DeepMind, and has moved into a chairman role of that unit. He has also assumed the chief scientist title.
The chief scientist role had been occupied by Jeff Dean. Dean has left the company after 27 years to start his own company with Google senior fellow Sanjay Ghemawat.
"I don't know that you're going to see it," Sheridan added on a potential negative impact to the business from Alphabet's brain drain. "I think they have a lot of talent. They have a very deep bench."
Concerns about AI spending have overshadowed a strong second quarter for Google parent company Alphabet.
The standout was Google Cloud, where revenue surged an eye-popping 82% to $24.8 billion, while the company's cloud backlog ballooned to $514 billion, underscoring the enormous demand for AI infrastructure.
Alphabet's second quarter capital expenditures came in at $44.9 billion, slightly above Wall Street forecasts of $44.7 billion. Full-year capital expenditures guidance was raised to $195 billion to $205 billion from $180 billion to $190 billion, with a "significant" increase seen for 2027, executives said on the earnings call.
